description.value: The Ranger Station Art Gallery occupies the original 1951 Forestry Ranger Station building on the shore of Harrison Lake, operated by the not-for-profit Kent Harrison Arts Council since 1972. It is the only public art gallery in the area, hosting monthly exhibitions by visual artists and running a year-long national artist-in-residence program with on-site living and studio space. Cyclists passing through Harrison Hot Springs can step into this historic building to catch rotating shows featuring a wide range of visual art media.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is detailed and clearly current, referencing the 2026 exhibition season and a 2027 application deadline. No bike-specific amenities (bike parking, washrooms, water refill) are mentioned anywhere on the site, so all three required criteria remain null. The visit-us page explicitly states 'The Arts Council no longer has a phone at the Gallery,' confirming the empty OSM phone field, and the address 98 Rockwell Dr, Harrison Hot Springs is corroborated by the website.
concerns: Gallery has no phone; website explicitly states 'The Arts Council no longer has a phone at the Gallery' — contact is email-only (khacinfo@gmail.com).
OSM seasonal=yes is confirmed; gallery operates reduced weekday-only hours mid-December to mid-February.
No bike-specific amenities (bike parking, washrooms, water) mentioned anywhere on the website; these fields could not be verified.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A well-established, actively operating public art gallery in a historic 1951 building on Harrison Lake — a legitimate and appealing cultural stop for touring cyclists in Harrison Hot Springs. Amenity evidence is thin but the attraction itself is a clear WWC fit.
enrichment_extras.notes: Email address recently changed to khacinfo@gmail.com, highlighted prominently across the website. Mailing address differs from physical address: Box 502, Agassiz BC V0M 1A0.
